The lab results are pending, but your description of specific sweet cravings combined with weight gain and behavioral changes is highly suggestive of a paraneoplastic syndrome. Could you tell me if you've noticed any skin darkening (hyperpigmentation) or fatigue recently? Also, have you experienced muscle weakness or difficulty standing up from a seated position?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Cortisol, ACTH, and Electrolytes.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your glucose, thyroid, and cortisol levels are normal, I need to rule out a pituitary issue causing excess growth hormone. Have you noticed any enlargement of your hands or feet, or deepening of your voice? REQUEST TEST: IGF-1, Prolactin, and MRI_Pituitary.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acromegaly (Growth Hormone Excess). While the initial screening tests were normal, the classic presentation of inappropriate behavior, specific food cravings (sweet/starchy), rapid weight gain, and physical changes like enlarged hands/feet strongly suggests a pituitary adenoma. The normal IGF-1 can occur in early stages; the MRI will confirm the presence of a pituitary tumor.
